title: Medical-grade buccal swabs versus drugstore cotton swabs: No difference in DNA yield
author: Ruiz, Chaney, et al.

steps.title: Collect buccal samples
steps.instruction: At 24‑hour intervals, swab the inside of the cheek for 15–30 seconds using the specified swab type and record the number of replicates.

substeps.instruction: Medical‑grade swabs: use Puritan Rectangular Foam Swabs (Cat. #25-1605; n = 15), Puritan Round Foam Swabs (Cat. #25-1805; n = 15), or Puritan HydraFlock® Flock Swabs (Cat. #25-3306-H; n = 12); collect from a single cheek because each swab has a cotton tip on only one end.
Standard cotton swabs (Q‑tips®; n = 8): swab both cheeks, using one cotton‑tipped end for each side, then combine the two ends into a single sample.
Store medical‑grade swabs in their original packaging; store cotton swabs in paper envelopes at room temperature (25 °C) for no more than one week before extraction.

steps.title: Extract DNA from swabs
steps.instruction: Use the QIAamp DNA Investigator Kit (Cat. #56504) with the “Isolation of DNA from Surface and Buccal Swabs” protocol on the QIAcube extraction robot (Qiagen, Germany) to isolate DNA from each collected sample.

steps.title: Quantify total DNA
steps.instruction: Measure total DNA yield with a Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer using the Broad Range DNA assay (Cat. #Q32853) following the manufacturer’s (Life Technologies, USA) guidelines.

steps.title: Quantify human DNA by qPCR
steps.instruction: Perform an Alu Ya5 qPCR assay on the total‑DNA extracts using PerfeCTa® SYBR® Green SuperMix ROX (Cat. #95055-500, Quanta BioSciences, USA) with primers forward 5′ GTCAGGAGATCGAGACCATCCC 3′ and reverse 5′ TCCTGCCTCAGCCTCCCAAG 3′ on a StepOnePlus instrument (Life Technologies, USA).

steps.title: Analyze data in R
steps.instruction: Import the Qubit fluorometer readings and qPCR results into the statistical program R and conduct the described ANOVA and post‑hoc analyses.
